page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the 64-bit ARM architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, relying on network-attached EBS storage and utilizing the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It provides a high baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the c6gn.8xlarge in the average tier for multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance scored 48,563.42, and the Geekbench multi-core score reached 11,689.0. Single-core performance is relatively weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 973.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,519.38. Memory bandwidth tests show 181.11 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 74.98 GB/sec for write operations. Cryptographic performance is supported by hardware-accelerated AES.

Given its 50 Gbps network bandwidth and compute-to-memory ratio, this instance is designed for network-intensive and compute-bound workloads. It performs well in multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation and static web serving. However, it is less suited for single-threaded tasks or large language model inference, where it exhibits weaker performance. The ARM64 architecture offers a cost-efficient alternative to traditional x86 instances by delivering balanced multi-core throughput and high network capacity at a lower resource-density cost.
